title: Experiment Runway: multi-variant A/B scheduler with rehearsal rollback and session affinity
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: teams running multi-variant A/B experiments and policy-driven canaries currently stitch together routing, rollouts, and replay logic across multiple controllers. This PR introduces 'Experiment Runway', a first-class orchestrator that sequences multi-variant experiments (A/B/n), supports weighted shadow traffic, session-affine variant routing, and a rehearsal-based rollback rehearsal step that validates rollback paths before exposing them to production traffic. Goals: (1) provide deterministic, auditable experiment lifecycles that reduce human error during variant swaps, (2) enable automatic rollback rehearsals to uncover failures in teardown/restore steps, (3) preserve session affinity for long-lived user sessions, preventing user experience drift when experiments change mid-session, and (4) surface clear telemetry and failure modes to Redwood Console. Summary of changes: Adds a new controller (experiment-runway) and a lightweight runtime adapter for multi-variant traffic shaping. Introduces a new Experiment CRD schema, per-variant safety gates (latency/error/regression thresholds), a rehearsal pipeline that runs teardown/rollback operations in a sandboxed shadow plane, and session-affinity cookies/token hashing integration. Includes e2e harness and smoke tests, console dashboard wiring, and Linear/Jira links to incident reproduction steps. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.feature.experiment_runway. We will ship in two stages: Stage 1 enable only in staging for internal experiments and run canary on Redwood-owned traffic; Stage 2 enable by opt-in in Dedicated customers after release notes and migration guide. Backwards compatibility: existing canary and shadow controllers are untouched; Experiment Runway is opt-in and can co-exist. See release_notes for migration guidance. Related work: builds on ENG-1304 (cohort fencing) and reuses metric-gates from ENG-1248.

review_thread: Jonah Kim: Nice direction. Two quick asks: (1) can you document the invariants the rehearsal runner promises? I worry about partial teardown leaving user sessions in a bad state, (2) please add a unit test for the hashing sticky cache eviction policy.

Maya Patel (author): Added an explicit invariants section in rehearsal_runner.go and added the sticky cache eviction unit test; see commits f2d88b2 and d44c1b0. The rehearsal runner will run teardown in a sandbox and only flip a 'rollback-ready' flag after snapshot verification succeeds to guard against partial-tear situations.

Priya Rao: The Experiment CRD validation looks good. Please ensure the UI does not expose weighted variants >100 without normalization. Also we need explicit metrics for rehearsal outcomes (success/failure/timeout).
Maya Patel: Normalization check added to CRD webhook and rehearsal metrics exported (observability/metrics added).
Evan Schultz: CI flaky on the e2e cluster repro — saw a timeout on roundtrip when the rehearsal sandboxpod scheduling was constrained. Could we add a scheduler priority class or a local fallback?
Maya Patel: Added scheduler priority class for rehearsal pods and a local fallback to run rehearsal as a lightweight in-proc replay when scheduling fails (see commit e12f7a6).
